item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: This was pretty much my issue - this is missing everything that made the first factory-format different and interesting. Where that article succeeded in portraying the inhuman perspective of the Factory, and its utter disregard for the value of human life, this is abandoned for a slapstick act, and hardly anything of interest transpires over the course of the article. I could see myself upvoting something like this, with the Factory handling a silly obstruction, but the progression was too dry and the writing too out-of-character for me to get immersed in what little story there actually is. -1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
As much as I want to answer this with my standard reply, this one was a disappointment, for a lot of reasons. The biggest thing is, the Factory's employees were characterized less like, well, how I feel Factory employees should be characterized and more like, Iunno, mooks from a cartoon aimed at Pre-K students?

I can imagine the carp hating the Factory but I don't see them being this effective. And a lot of what I liked about the first Factory memo was how damn evil they were without coming across as cartoonish. What I think does this one in is, giving the employees voices at all. Factory employees should not really be employees; to the Factory, they're equipment, property. The only voice they should have is the one the Factory gives them.

Iunno, sorry I had to break our running joke for this one.

This is what happens when you piss off the paladin carp. They get revenge.

Our friends here have been mentioned in KoI-Format; that "unusually colored" carp with the harpoon (the carpoon, if you will) is none other than The Spear of Clear Water herself. When I first drafted this, I was actually intending for it to be that tench-koi hybrid messing with The Factory, but paladin carp are so much more fun.
